statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119591 is a stack exhaustion in SQLite's count-of-view optimization: count(*) over a view built on a large multi-row VALUES clause produces a deeply nested expression whose recursive freeing in sqlite3ExprDeleteNN() exhausts the C stack, so SQL or a crafted view in a database file can crash the process. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-10-04T05:34:47Z. The fix is trunk check-in https://sqlite.org/src/info/ab621a3e11ee4acc, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/eff50a067c55f972909e7780e506e91382d08de2, which makes countOfViewOptimization() in src/select.c discard the generated expression once the parser has recorded an error; it has no counterpart on the 3.53 maintenance branch. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of that check-in. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. We ran the test with the sqlite3 shell, and with a test program linked once against the shared library and once against the static archive, for every build on x86_64 and aarch64. With a 1 MiB stack, SELECT count(*) over a view of 200,000 VALUES rows crashes with a segmentation fault in 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0, and fails cleanly with "Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 1000)" in 3.53.4-r1, on both architectures and in all three copies. The x86_64 runs used Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
